Seasonal floods along a river network

Source: R/river.R
river_floods.Rd

Probabilities that each site of a river network loses all its populations at each step because of floods, for disturbance in simulate_metacommunity(). Each period (a year) has a flood season of flood_steps steps, starting at step start of the period, and a flood happens in a given year with probability year_prob, so that years differ. During a flood, the probability of washout at a site is proportional to its size relative to the largest site raised to size_effect, scaled so that the most exposed site has probability probability: positive values make floods harsher in large rivers, negative values in headwaters (flashier floods in small, steep streams), and 0 the same everywhere.

Usage

river_floods(
  landscape,
  n_steps,
  period,
  flood_steps = 1,
  start = 1,
  probability = 0.5,
  size_effect = 1,
  size = "upstream_length",
  year_prob = 1
)

Arguments

landscape

A landscape from landscape_river().

n_steps

Number of steps: one whole number, 1 or more.

period

Steps per year: one whole number, 1 or more.

flood_steps

Steps of the flood season in each year: one whole number, from 1 up to period.

start

Step of the year at which the flood season begins: one whole number, from 1 up to period.

probability

Probability of washout during a flood at the most exposed site: one number between 0 and 1.

size_effect

Exponent of the relative size of each site: one finite number.

size

Size of each site: "upstream_length" (the default, a proxy for catchment area and discharge), "magnitude" (Shreve magnitude) or a positive numeric vector with one value per site.

year_prob

Probability that a flood happens in a year: one number between 0 and 1.

Value

A matrix of probabilities with one row per site and one column per step, with an attribute flood_years, the years in which a flood happened.

Details

Floods here remove populations; to change the environment during floods instead, use env_pulse() on the sites and steps of the flood.

See also

Other landscapes: dispersal_kernel(), env_over_time(), env_pulse(), env_river(), env_seasonal(), env_space_time(), landscape_grid(), landscape_implicit(), landscape_matrix(), landscape_points(), landscape_river(), river_covariance(), river_network()

Examples

set.seed(1)
land <- landscape_river(river_network(30))
floods <- river_floods(land, n_steps = 200, period = 20, flood_steps = 2,
                       probability = 0.3, year_prob = 0.7)
attr(floods, "flood_years")
#> [1] 1 3 4 5 7 8 9
# the mainstem floods more than the headwaters
tapply(apply(floods, 1, max), land$network$headwater, mean)
#>      FALSE       TRUE 
#> 0.08136869 0.01041697 
traits <- data.frame(optimum = 50, sigma = 30, r_max = 3, row.names = "sp1")
sim <- simulate_metacommunity(land, traits, matrix(0.05, dimnames = list("sp1", "sp1")),
                              n_steps = 200, disturbance = floods)
